title: Quantitative proteomic assessment of very early cellular signaling events: qPACE
protocol: Label your cells with SILAC for at least 5 population doublings to ensure complete incorporation of isotope-labeled amino acids.
Serum-starve your cells before pumping for approximately 12 hours.
Connect pumps P1 and P2 with tubing, running them at the same speed of 800 μl/min.
Pump P1 delivers medium containing the stimulus.
Pump P2 delivers cells in suspension or growing on microcarrier beads.
Run pump P3 at a speed of 8 ml/min to deliver the quenching reagent, which is 80% ethanol prechilled to -20°C.
Adjust the tube length according to your pumping speed and tubing diameter to reach the desired stimulation time.
Use 1 mm i.d. Teflon tubes with lengths of 3.4 cm for 1 second, 17 cm for 5 seconds, 34 cm for 10 seconds, and 204 cm for 60 seconds.
Prepare cell suspension with 1.5-4×10^8 cells per time point resuspended in 5 or 10 ml of medium.
Prepare double-concentrated stimulation medium containing 300 ng/ml EGF to achieve a final concentration of 150 ng/ml.
Pump the sample through the system.
Pellet cells by centrifugation.
Discard supernatant.
Wash pellet with ice-cold PBS.
Pellet cells again.
Lysate cells with lysing buffer containing protease and phosphatase inhibitors.
Immunoprecipitate complexes of interest.
Separate immunoprecipitated complexes by SDS-PAGE.
Digest separated proteins enzymatically, e.g., with trypsin.
Enrich phosphopeptides prior to LC-MS analysis, e.g., using TiO2.
Analyze resulting peptide mixture by LC-MS.
Quantitate peptides of interest, e.g., using MSQuant software.
